Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And regarding the sons of Adam it is likewise said: "and You say: Return," for the Blessed Name arouses them to repent through the Heavenly Voice: "Return, O backsliding children" (Yirmiyah 3:14); which is an utterance whispered in internal arousal within the heart from the fact that they are "the children of Adam"; who possess the holy soul-root of Adam who was created in the Divine Image and Likeness (Bereishis 1:26); which is the likeness upon the Throne resembling the appearance of a Man (Yechezkel 1:26), being the visage of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, the root of Israel. — ‘upper teshuvah’ — and [before it] the yetzer departs.”
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: “And the earth was unformed and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep.” It is stated in the Gemara (Chagigah 12a): “‘Tohu’ is a green line encircling the entire world from which darkness issues; ‘bohu’ refers to the moist/slimy stones sunken in the abyss from which water issues.” The meaning of this is: Tohu is the opposite of the attribute of Chesed (Lovingkindness)—for Chesed represents the wide, unrestricted expansion of divine bounty; while Tohu is the reverse, signifying dread: creation trembled to pour forth bounty to be placed under human dominion.

Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Pesachim 88b: ‘We learned in the mishna: If a slave forgot which animal his master had specified and therefore offered a lamb and a kid with a stipulation, and his master also forgot what he said to him, neither animal may be used. Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: This embodies the spiritual level of our forefather Jacob, peace be upon him, who termed the Sanctuary a "House" (Bayit), as our Sages of blessed memory stated in Pesachim (88a); for as is known, the attribute of "give truth to Jacob" corresponds to the transcendent Name Havayah, which constitutes a permanent, enduring house. [Therefore, in the Holy Temple, the High Priest would pronounce the Name Havayah according to its letters, and likewise the priests in the Sanctuary,] because anything possessing temporal bounds is termed a temporary tent (ohel arai), which ceases to exist once its bounded allotment is exhausted.

And this is a valid proof, for in no other language do "copper" and "serpent" form an intrinsic paronomasia (pun); why then did Moses fashion it of copper? Perforce because the primary language of Torah and of the Blessed Name was Hebrew.

Nevertheless strict justice dictates: as man constricts himself according to his finite strength, Hashem rewards him according to His infinite power, defrauding no creature of its reward. For since creation exists solely through divine Will and not philosophical necessity, and all is grace, there is no disparity before Him between a high rung and a lowly one, neither being compulsory unto Him.

Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And this perception is attained through the spiritual reality of the Holy Temple, which embodies the permanent and eternally established consciousness, just like the Sabbath; which is why a non-Jew who observes the Sabbath is liable to death, etc. (as stated in Sanhedrin 58b), and the Sages noted (Shabbat 10b): "[Hashem said to Moses:] 'I have a precious gift in My treasury... Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: Therefore, because they desired man's creation and emerged through his prayer, at their root they possess an enduring imprint of eternal life. Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: And this explains the Gemara's challenge from "Blessed be the glory of Hashem from His place" [Ezekiel 3:12], which resolves: that praise was uttered by the Ophanim who belong to the Throne of Glory (see Tosafot there, and see what I wrote below in chapter 4), from the Supernal World whence the souls of Israel are hewn, wherefore their spiritual rank mirrors that of Israel; and the second resolution: "once permission was given" (Chullin 91b), meaning once divine recognition was initiated below by Israel, the angels are also enabled to perceive; and understand this.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: And why did it not compare them to “a lamp in broad daylight”? However, stating “like a candle before a torch” indicates that the Blessed Name preserves value for human labor even when His vast supernal light is unveiled; for a single candle forms an integral part of the torch, since from the joining of many candles a great torch is formed.

Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: As parabled in Sifrei (Ha'azinu 309): A man bequeathed ten fields by his father, who purchased one field of his own, loved that single field more than all the inherited ones. Kisvei_Rav_Tzadok_Parallel_Translation: Therefore the letter Aleph rests as a silent, quiescent letter after all vowel movements, such as: u-va (after kamatz), reishit (after tzeireh), rosh (after cholam), rishon (after chirik), chattat (after patach), hu (after shuruk), pe'arah (after segol). For absolute oneness is not circumscribed by space, but rather all space resides within it, as the Sages of blessed memory stated (Bereishit Rabbah 68:9) regarding the Blessed Name Who is called Makom ("Place"), for the Holy One, blessed be He, is the place of the universe.
Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: And this is “In the beginning Elohim created”—this Name gives strength to the worlds so they do not collapse like the shattered worlds. As taught in Midrash Rabbah (9:2): The Holy One built worlds and destroyed them, saying: “This one pleases Me, those did not.” The explanation is that the shattered worlds collapsed because they lacked the constricting attribute, expanding with unchecked intensity until they shattered into nonexistence.

And in the future, when both opposing corruptions—anger and lust—are purified, the complete redemption will dawn.

Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: Wherefore when promised survival for himself and his sons, it did not occur to his mind that there was room to petition for more. Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: And this mirrors the intrinsic sanctity of the Sabbath, as the Talmud states (Beitzah 17a): that the sanctity of Shabbat is fixed and established by God even if Israel does not sanctify it. Primary_Source_Translation_And_Context: Zohar, Balak 199a: “In the Zohar (Balak III 199a), on ‘He shone forth from Mount Paran’ (Deuteronomy 33:2), it is taught that before giving the Torah to Israel, the Holy One, blessed be He, offered it to the children of Esau on Mount Seir, who rejected it because it is written therein ‘You shall not murder,’ and to the children of Ishmael, who rejected it because it is written therein ‘You shall not steal / commit adultery.’” Context and connection to Kometz HaMinchah: In Kometz HaMinchah 2:79, Rav Tzadok draws upon this kabbalistic teaching (Zohar, Balak 199a) to illuminate his teaching here (“As stated in the Zohar, Parashat Balak 199, concerning "He shone forth from Seir": what is written concerning it? Kisvei_Beis_Ishbitz_Radzin_Parallel_Tran: For to this points the Vav of “And you shall not murder”—meaning constrict your boundary for the sake of the peaceful settlement of the world; yet nonetheless “and you shall not commit adultery”—do not overstep your boundary in seeking to populate the world excessively such that you enter the domain of adultery, for you must give harmonious connection to “and you shall not commit adultery” as well.
